extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients, institutional grants management officials (GMOs), principal investigators, and research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Policy guidance describing what costs and activities are allowable, allocable, and reasonable on NIH grants; documentation, allocation, and specific-item rules for recipients and their subrecipients/consortium participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost transfers — documentation and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain documentation of cost transfers pursuant to 2 CFR Part 200.337; an explanation merely stating the transfer was made 'to correct error' or 'to transfer to correct project' is not sufficient; transfers solely to cover cost overruns are not allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should have systems to detect errors within a reasonable timeframe; untimely discovery may indicate poor internal controls. Frequent cost-recording errors may indicate need for accounting system improvements or enhanced internal controls. NIH may require corrective action or impose additional award terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: GMO monitoring of expenditure rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The GMO monitors recipient expenditure rates under individual grants within each budget period and overall project period to ensure expenditures are consistent with the approved project and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may question or restrict expenditures inconsistent with expectations. GMO may review cash drawdowns to detect accelerated/delayed expenditure patterns that could indicate deficient financial management or internal controls and may seek information or make adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs and closely related work
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost that benefits two or more projects/activities in proportions that can be determined without undue effort should be allocated on the basis of proportional benefit; costs that benefit multiple projects but proportions cannot be determined may be allocated on any reasonable basis provided costs are allowable, allocable, and reasonable and the recipient’s financial management system has adequate internal controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequate internal controls example: no single person has complete control over all aspects of a financial transaction. Allocation must follow applicable cost principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable credits — treatment on FFR
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicable credits (e.g., purchase discounts, rebates, recoveries, adjustments) operate to offset or reduce direct or indirect cost items and must be treated as an adjustment on the recipient’s FFR whether those credits accrue during or after the period of grant support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cost principles for additional information. NIH awarding IC will notify recipients of any additional actions necessary regarding applicable credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services provided by affiliated organizations — allowability conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by an affiliated but separate legal entity (e.g., a foundation) in support of a recipient foundation are allowable for reimbursement under NIH grants only if at least one of the following conditions is met: (1) the affiliated organization is charged for and legally obligated to pay for services provided by the parent organization; (2) state/local law prescribes how Federal reimbursement will be expended and requires approval by a state/local official; or (3) there is a valid written agreement permitting the recipient foundation to retain Federal reimbursement of parent organization costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of these conditions are met, parent-organization service costs are not allowable for reimbursement but may be acceptable for cost-sharing. Foundations representing existing recipients should contact DGP, OPERA before seeking separate recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: General allowability of costs/activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowability is governed by the cost principles; NIH-specific requirements and award terms/conditions may take precedence. If a cost is allowable it is allocable as either direct or indirect depending on the recipient’s accounting system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section is not all-inclusive; consult cost principles. An award based on an application that included costs/activities requiring NIH prior approval constitutes prior approval for those items; post-award requests for prior-approval items not described in the approved application are subject to change-in-project/budget rules. Recipients with questions should contact the GMO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium participants and contractors under grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Consortium participants and contractors under grants are subject to the cost principles applicable to their organization type and to any recipient-imposed requirements necessary for compliance with NIH award terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortium arrangements to carry out programmatic effort or procure routine goods/services may require NIH approval per change-in-project/budget requirements; see procurement system standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profit/fee policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost principles do not address profit or fee. NIH allows payment of fee on SBIR/STTR grants only; NIH will not provide profit or fee to any other recipient type under any other grant program or support mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fee may not be paid by a recipient to a consortium participant (including a for-profit). However, a fee (profit) may be paid to a contractor providing routine goods or services under a grant in accordance with normal commercial practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising and Public Relations — allowable uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising costs mean costs of advertising media and related administrative costs. The only allowable advertising costs are those solely for: (a) recruitment of personnel required for performance of a Federal award; (b) procurement of goods and services for performance of a Federal award; (c) disposal of scrap or surplus materials acquired in performance of a Federal award (with exceptions); or (d) program outreach and other specific purposes necessary to meet award requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public relations (community relations) costs are allowable only when: (a) specifically required by the Federal award; (b) communicating with the public/press about specific activities/accomplishments resulting from award performance; or (c) conducting liaison with news media/government public relations limited to keeping the public informed on matters of public concern. Unallowable items include all other advertising/public relations costs, costs of unrelated meetings/conventions (displays, meeting rooms, salaries for exhibit setup), promotional items/souvenirs, and advertising designed solely to promote the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alcoholic beverages
rubrics_metrics.description: Alcoholic beverages are unallowable as an entertainment expense, but are allowable if within the scope of an approved research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as unallowable entertainment unless explicitly part of approved project scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration and Renovation (A&R) — allowability and documentation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual A&R projects treated as direct costs and determined to be minor are subject to A&R policies; major A&R are subject to Construction Grants chapter. Routine maintenance is not considered A&R. Certain installation costs may be considered equipment or A&R depending on accounting system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A&R must meet criteria: building useful life consistent with program purposes; A&R essential to grant project purpose; space occupied by project; space suitable for human occupancy before A&R unless purpose differs; if rented, lease terms compatible and cover project period. If A&R affects a historic site, preservation requirements must be followed. Recipients may rebudget up to 25% of total approved budget for a budget period into A&R without NIH prior approval unless rebudgeting results in a change in scope or addition of a major A&R project. Under foreign grants, major A&R is unallowable; minor A&R generally allowable unless prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs for acquisition, care, use, and rehoming/retirement of experimental animals are allowable contingent upon compliance with the PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recipient operates an animal resource facility, charges should follow the Cost Analysis and Rate Setting Manual for Animal Resource Facilities. See Public Policy Requirements and Objectives—Animal Welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audiovisual activities — allowability, production, submission, and acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Production costs for audiovisuals (visual imagery, sound, multimedia, exhibits) are allowable. Recipients with in-house production should assess efficiency of in-house vs. contracting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If audiovisual intended for general public is produced under NIH-supported project, recipient must submit two copies of finished product with annual or final progress report; costs of such copies allowable. Audiovisuals must bear an acknowledgment and disclaimer (example wording provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit services — allowable costs and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A reasonably proportionate share of costs of audits required by the Single Audit Act (31 U.S.C. 7501-7507) and 2 CFR Part 200 are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unallowable: audit costs when audits required by Single Audit Act/Subpart F have not been conducted or not in accordance with requirements, and costs of auditing entities exempted due to expenditures < $1,000,000. Financial statement audit costs of a recipient or subrecipient without a Federal award may be included in indirect cost pool. Pass-through entities may charge Federal awards for agreed-upon-procedures engagements to monitor subrecipients if (a) conducted in accordance with GAGAS or applicable international attestation standards, (b) paid/arranged by pass-through entity, and (c) limited in scope to certain compliance requirements (allowed/unallowed activities; allowable costs/cost principles; eligibility; reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Bad debts (uncollectable debts), including losses from uncollectable accounts and related collection/legal costs after declared uncollectable, are unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2 CFR Part 200.428 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonding costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonding costs arise when the Federal awarding agency requires assurance against financial loss (bids, performance, payment, advance payment, infringement, fidelity bonds) or when recipient requires similar assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs of bonding required pursuant to Federal award terms are allowable. Costs of bonding required by the recipient in general operations are allowable as an indirect cost to the extent they follow sound business practice and rates/premiums are reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Books and journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable. If an organization has a library, books and journals generally should be provided as part of normal library services and treated as indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Building acquisition is unallowable unless specifically authorized by program legislation and provided for in the Notice of Award (NoA). For real property acquired with NIH grant support, title insurance may be charged in proportion to the Federal share; filing fees for recording Federal interest may be charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Construction Grants—Allowable and Unallowable Costs and Activities in IIB for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital expenditures — rules of allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital expenditures for general purpose equipment, buildings, and land are unallowable as direct charges except with prior written approval; capital expenditures for special purpose equipment are allowable as direct costs provided items relating to a change in scope (often indicated by unit cost $25,000 or more) have prior written approval; capital expenditures for improvements that materially increase value/useful life are unallowable as direct cost except with prior written approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When approved as direct charges, capital expenditures will be charged in the period incurred or as negotiated. Unamortized portion of equipment written off due to change in capitalization may be recovered by continuing depreciation claims or amortizing per negotiation. Costs of disposal or transfer of equipment at NIH direction are allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative costs specifically associated with award closeout (e.g., salaries preparing final reports, publication/printing, disposition of equipment/property, related indirect costs) are allowable without NIH prior approval and may be incurred until the due date of final report(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incurred closeout costs must be liquidated before the due date of the final report(s) and charged to the final budget period unless NIH specifies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of improper payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs to recover improper payments are allowable as direct or indirect costs, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts collected may be used by recipient in accordance with cash management standards in 2 CFR Part 200.305. See Improper Payment section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable. Includes local and long-distance telephone calls, express mail, and postage, and usually treated as indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium agreements/contracts under grants — allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable to carry out a portion of the programmatic effort or for acquisition of routine goods/services under the grant; such arrangements may require NIH approval per Administrative Requirements—Changes in Project and Budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See procurement system standards and Consortium Agreements chapter in IIB for applicable policies when collaborating with other organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction (new facility or major projects such as relocation of exterior walls/roofs/floors, attachment of fire escapes, completion of unfinished shell space) is allowable only when program legislation specifically authorizes new construction/modernization or major A&R and NIH specifically authorizes such costs in the NoA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Construction Grants chapter in IIB for procedures and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contingency reserves or similar payments for events that cannot be foretold with certainty are unallowable under non-construction grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contingency funds do not include pension funds, self-insurance funds, and normal accruals. See Construction Grants chapter for contingency funds under construction grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customs and import duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Customs and import duties are unallowable? (text: Unallowable.) — but note guidance: allowable under domestic grants when performance within U.S., its possessions, or territories, or when foreign involvement is incidental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charges may include consular fees, customs surtaxes, VATs, and related charges. See Taxes in this exhibit. (The document states 'Unallowable.' then discusses allowability under certain circumstances; recipients should consult the specific rule in context or contact GMO.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation or use allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Depreciation or use charges are allowable and usually treated as indirect costs. Depreciation on equipment or buildings acquired under a federally supported project are not allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See related categories: Capital Expenditures, Equipment, Special Purpose Equipment, Acquisition Cost, Capital Assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable as payment to volunteers or research subjects who contribute bodily samples (blood, urine, tissues) specifically project-related. Donor costs are not considered research patient care expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Incentive Costs in this exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drugs
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable if within scope of an approved research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project funds may not be used to purchase drugs classified by FDA as 'ineffective' or 'possibly effective' except in approved clinical research projects or where no alternative exists other than therapy with 'possibly effective' drugs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dues or membership fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable as an indirect cost for organizational membership in business, professional, or technical organizations or societies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual membership dues may be allowable as a fringe benefit or employee development cost if paid according to established institutional policy and consistently applied regardless of funding source. See Membership, Subscription, and Professional Activity costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertainment costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of entertainment (amusement, diversion, social activities and associated costs like gifts) are unallowable unless they have a specific and direct programmatic purpose and are included in a Federal award or have prior written NIH approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fines, penalties, damages, and settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs resulting from violations or alleged violations of law/regulations are unallowable, except when incurred as a result of compliance with specific provisions of the Federal award or with prior written NIH approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits — general allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe benefits (leave, insurance, pensions, unemployment benefit plans, etc.) are allowable provided the benefits are reasonable and required by law, an organization-employee agreement, or established policy of the recipient or subrecipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided in 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart E; fringe benefit costs are allowable and should be evaluated for reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition remission and student compensation — conditions for allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuition remission and other compensation paid as or in lieu of wages to students under research grants are allowable provided: (1) the individual conducts activities necessary to the Federal award; (2) provided in accordance with established institutional policy and consistently applied; (3) during academic period student is enrolled in an advanced degree program and activities relate to the degree; (4) tuition/payments are reasonable compensation and conditioned on performance of necessary work; (5) IHE practice is to similarly compensate students under Federal awards and other activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charges are subject to reporting requirements in 2 CFR Part 200.430(i). NIH will determine allowability and reasonableness under 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits — insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Insurance is usually treated as an indirect cost. Special insurance required as condition of grant may be charged as a direct cost if consistent with organizational policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical liability (malpractice) insurance is allowable only if research involves human subjects; it must be treated as a direct cost and assigned to individual grants based on insurer allocation. Insurance for equipment normally included in indirect costs but may be direct if organizational policy dictates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits — leave criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of fringe benefits in the form of regular compensation during authorized leave (annual, family-related, sick, holidays, court, military, etc.) are allowable if: (1) provided under established written leave policies; (2) costs are equitably allocated to all related activities including Federal awards; and (3) the accounting basis selected for costing each type of leave is consistently followed by the recipient or a specified group of employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NRSA chapters for specific trainee/fellow leave policy references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits — pension plan costs and funding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Pension plan costs incurred in accordance with established written policies are allowable provided policies are reasonable, allocation methods not discriminatory, accrual-based accounting follows GAAP, and costs are funded for plan participants within six months after the end of the fiscal year. Additional detailed rules address pay-as-you-go vs actuarial methods, funding timing, use of excess amounts, amortization of unfunded liability on conversion, and charging of unfunded pension costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific provisions include: (a) pay-as-you-go limited to actual payments to retirees; (b) actuarial cost methods allowable if funded within six months (or later period agreed by cognizant agency); (c) excess funding may be used in future periods; (d) conversion to actuarial method allows amortization of unfunded liability if GAAP-compliant; (e) unfunded pension payments must be charged per allocation principles of 2 CFR 200.431; (f) recipient must provide Federal cognizant agency required information. Recipients may elect recognized actuarial methods and consult cognizant agency for indirect cost matters.
